newsitem.title: UK: Mideast clean tanker rates up, U.S. very quiet.
newsitem.headline: Mideast clean tanker rates up, U.S. very quiet.

text.p: Clean product tanker chartering rates were broadly unchanged this week, with Middle East to Asia rates edging up and Caribbean upcoast trips slipping.

Shipping brokers said there was no rush to fix tonnage ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday and Caribbean upcoast trips on 30,000 tonners actually fell to W165 from W180. The last representative fixture of the Danila was at W189 on 27,000 tonne a day or so ago, pro-rating to W170 on 30,000 tonnes.
"Owners jumped on the first piece of business to come their way rather than be left without any turkey," said leading shipbrokers E.A. Gibson in a report.
In the Middle East Gulf to Japan market rates on 55,000 tonners rose to W197.5 with further potential for increases seen.
"Tonnage is looking just a bit tight, which added to some good charterering interest suggests rates will breach W200," said one shipbroker.

Mediterranean markets were slower. Algeria's port of Skikda closed on Tuesday due to bad weather and remained closed on Friday. Shipbrokers said this might start to lead to delays, but so far most owners have been able to avoid the port.
Mediterranean trips on 27,500 tonne naphtha carriers was steady around W175, but gas oil tankers carrying 30,000 tonne cargoes had to contend with W140-145, said Gibson.

The UK/cont 20,000 tonners were pegged around W225 although at the tail end of the week most fixing was concentrated on larger sized ships. There were several fixtures to the U.S on 25,000 and 28,000 tonne cargoes as well as UK/cont to Med trips.
